preamble: Each domain question draws from the complete medical record. Points reflect diagnostic weight. Cost reflects typical test burden: Small = existing record / standard labs  |  Medium = targeted test ($200–$1,500)  |  Large = genetic or complement panel ($1,500–$5,000+)  |  ⚠ ADAMTS13 must be drawn BEFORE plasma exchange — most time-sensitive test in TMA.

questions.question: Is microangiopathic hemolytic anemia (MAHA) confirmed? (Hgb <10 g/dL + schistocytes >1% on peripheral smear + elevated LDH + low haptoglobin)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — MAHA confirmed; all four TMA criteria present on CBC, smear, LDH, and haptoglobin

questions.question: Is thrombocytopenia present (platelets <150,000/μL, preferably <100,000/μL)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — thrombocytopenia confirmed; essential TMA triad component

questions.question: Is severe acute kidney injury (AKI) present with oliguria/anuria, or has renal replacement therapy (dialysis) been initiated?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe AKI (KDIGO Stage 2–3) or dialysis-requiring confirmed

questions.question: Are CNS symptoms present (seizures, encephalopathy, focal neurological deficits)? CNS involvement more common in aHUS than typical HUS — poor prognostic sign
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — CNS involvement confirmed; indicates severe TMA with extrarenal spread

questions.question: Is ADAMTS13 activity >10%? (ADAMTS13 <10% = TTP — NOT aHUS; this finding negates the aHUS diagnosis)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — ADAMTS13 >10% confirmed; TTP excluded; aHUS diagnosis supported

questions.question: Is there evidence of complement dysregulation? (low C3 + low factor H + elevated sC5b-9 — the aHUS alternative pathway activation pattern; C4 typically normal)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — complement dysregulation pattern confirmed: low C3, low factor H, elevated sC5b-9

questions.question: Has genetic testing identified a pathogenic variant in a complement regulatory gene (CFH, CFI, MCP/CD46, CFB, C3, THBD, DGKE)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — P/LP complement gene variant confirmed; or anti-factor H antibodies detected (acquired aHUS)

questions.question: Are Shiga toxin assay and STEC stool culture both negative? (excludes typical STEC-associated HUS)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — Shiga toxin and STEC culture negative; typical HUS excluded

questions.question: Is there no TMA-inducing medication in recent history? (quinine, calcineurin inhibitors, gemcitabine, bevacizumab)
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — no TMA-inducing medications identified on medication reconciliation

high.label: 🔴  ≥80 High confidence aHUS
high.action: initiate complement blockade with eculizumab (anti-C5) immediately; ensure meningococcal vaccination or prophylactic penicillin before first dose; nephrology and hematology co-management; genetic panel to guide long-term treatment duration

moderate.label: 🟡  60–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: consider empirical eculizumab while awaiting complement genetics and STEC results; do not delay treatment in critically ill patients; complete ADAMTS13, complement studies, and exclusion workup

low.label: 🟢  <60 Low confidence
low.action: additional testing required before aHUS diagnosis; ensure ADAMTS13, complement studies, and STEC testing are completed; consider alternative TMA diagnoses (TTP, drug-induced TMA, DIC, HELLP)
